newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Feb 5 - Partial data available indicate CPO production in January fell seasonally by 60,000 tonnes or 9.5 percent to an estimated 578,000 tonnes. The decline is marginally more than our previous tentative estimate. An early cessation of monsoon rains in East Malaysia during the month helped minimised interruptions in harvesting operations and ensured the overall drop in CPO production in Sabah was modest. Some producers in Sabah even managed to chalk up slight increases in production. CPO offtake fell substantally by nearly 170,000 tonnes to estimated 638,000 tonnes in January.

The extend of the contraction in exports was within our expectations although in the last week of January there were fears in the market that palm oil exports for the whole month would slump to not more than 500,000 tonnes. With demand continuing to exceed production, stocks of palm oil were further drawn down to an estimated 725,000 tonnes at end January or little changed from our estimate on January 21. The stocks were however much lower than the monthago level of 792,700 tonnes and the year ago level of 826,400 tonnes.

The bulk of the reduction in stocks was in the form of CPO which amounted to an estimated 375,000 tonnes as against 435,400 tonnes at end-December and 494,700 tonnes at end January '96. Stocks of CPO in the country during this month are likely to be further drawn down to less than 300,000 tonnes. However, the CPO stocks/usage ratio would not be much worse off from that in January. For one thing most palm oil mills and refineries are scheduled to be shut down for the same number of days during the Chinese New Year and Hari Raya holidays in February 7-10.

Some plants would be closed for a longer period of up to one week. CPO price average 1,315.50 ringgit in Jan, up from 1,223 ringgit in Dec and 1,245 ringgit in Jan '96. We expect price in the Jan-Mar quarter to average 1,300 ringgit or six percent higher than same period last year. March and April CPO futures settled at 1,325 ringgit and 1,305 ringgit yesterday, up from 1,266 ringgit and 1,256 ringgit respectively on Jan 20. RBD olein March and April/June were quoted at $595 and $585.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
